name: Background
summary: In the product app the page is white. Light grey is for surfaces inside or beside the white page, Vivid Pink at 5% is for hover and selected states plus at most one highlighted panel per screen, and black is for full-screen presenting and video or image viewers only. There is no dark mode, no tinted status surface and no gradient fill, and every non-white background comes from an --aha-bg-* token.
highlights: The page is white; light grey only inside or beside it
Vivid Pink at 5% for hover and selected, plus one highlighted panel per screen
Black only for presenting and viewers; no dark mode, no status tint, no gradient
Every non-white background is an --aha-bg-* token
whenToRead: Read before giving any product surface a background that is not white: a grey area, a pale pink panel, a dark screen, a status banner or a Splash background.
lead: This pattern is the product-app reading of the AhaSlides colour rules. The rules themselves live once, in brand/colour-rules.json, and are published on the Brand colour rules page (foundations/brand-colour-rules.html) and in the colour-rules.md feed; each rule below names the rule it applies (`source`) and the judge criterion that checks it. It ships no component. Presenter and customer content (a slide, an uploaded image, a presenter's own theme) is exempt, so the slide on the presenting stage is theme-coloured by design: see the canvas guideline. Web pages built from full-width sections, video, social posts, ads, slides and print follow the same rules page under their own environment, not this pattern.

skillRef.note: The enforceable criteria are anti-slop/criteria.json surfaces.background (C1 to C8). They and the rules below cite brand/colour-rules.json by rule id, so the rule text has one home.

componentBacklog: No missing components. The DS has no AI-gradient token yet: the AI feature's border gradient is the one gradient allowed, but until a token lands it cannot be expressed token-only. Add it here before a consumer needs it.

rules.rule: Keep the page, and every neutral container on it (card body, panel, modal and drawer body, table and list row, tab panel), white or unset (--aha-bg-container). Never paint one with a brand, pastel or other colour for emphasis.

Use light grey (--aha-bg-layout, --aha-bg-container-secondary) only for a surface that sits inside or beside the white page: a card, a sidebar, an input field, a table header, the editor workspace around the slide. Never make grey the background of a whole page, of the layout body behind the content, or of a full-width section.

Use Vivid Pink at 5% (--aha-bg-accent) for a hover or selected state, and for at most one highlighted panel per screen of the product app. A web page built from full-width sections (a help article, a sign-up or upgrade page) may use pale pink sections instead, under rules 3.2 to 3.5.
Use a black background (--aha-bg-dark) in two places only: full-screen presenting, and a video or image viewer.

Build no dark mode: no theme switch, no dark theme class, no prefers-color-scheme: dark restyle. People who need a dark screen use their device or browser setting, and the screen must not break under it.

Never tint a surface red, yellow, green or blue to show danger, warning, success or information. A status surface stays white and carries its meaning with an icon, clear wording and an outline or a black fill. The correct and wrong answer tints are not status colours: they fill an answer row, a response box or a result banner or chip, and nothing else.

Use no linear-, radial- or conic-gradient as a background or fill. The one exception is an AI feature: the gradient sits on the border (border-box) and the fill stays white (padding-box). The animated Skeleton shimmer between the neutral greys --aha-bg-hover, --aha-bg-container-secondary and --aha-split is not a gradient fill.

Bind every non-white background to a DS token (--aha-bg-layout, --aha-bg-container-secondary, --aha-bg-hover, --aha-bg-accent, --aha-bg-dark), never a raw #hex, rgb() or hsl() literal, even when the literal is the right colour.

Use a Splash background only on an empty state or a hero area, never on a dense screen such as the editor. Take the file from the Background library, or build it for the exact frame with build-splash.mjs; never draw, place, stretch or recolour the hooks by hand.

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern: the DS ships no background wrapper. The rule lives in the consuming app's styles; this pattern is the conventions plus the binary criteria (anti-slop/criteria.json, surfaces.background) a consumer self-judges against.

selfCheck.label: the page and every neutral container is white or unset

Vivid Pink at 5% only as a hover or selected fill, plus at most one highlighted panel per screen
black only for full-screen presenting and a video or image viewer; no dark mode
no status surface is tinted red, yellow, green or blue
no gradient background or fill, except the AI feature's border
every non-white background is an --aha-bg-* token, never a raw colour literal
a Splash background only on an empty state or a hero area, from the Background library
